07Vault & Gear
Operator

VaultCards you hold that aren’t in the loadout.

CardDomainLevelRecall

You can have five cards active at once: your loadout. The rest are in your vault, on your sheet but switched off. During any rest you can rearrange freely. Mid-scene, you can pull a card from the vault into the loadout by marking Stress equal to its recall cost; it replaces a card of your choice. A recall cost of 0 means it swaps for free. Until level 5 you'll rarely have more than five, and it won't matter. After that, the loadout is where your character's shape shows.

09Level Up
Operator

LevelHeavy boxes: a new Experience at +2 and +1 Proficiency.

1T12T23T24T25T36T37T38T49T410T4

When You Level Up

  1. Tier achievements. At level 2, 5, and 8: add a new Experience at +2 and gain +1 Proficiency. At 5 and 8, clear the marks on your traits so you can raise them again.
  2. Choose two advancements from your tier's list below, or from any earlier tier. Each has limited picks per tier; tick the box.
  3. Take a domain card of your level or lower from one of your domains.
  4. Raise both damage thresholds by 1. You always add your level to your armor's base thresholds.

AdvancementsTwo per level. Tick a box when you take one.

AdvancementTier 2Tier 3Tier 4
Traits. +1 to two unmarked traits; mark them.
Hit Points. One permanent Hit Point slot.
Stress. One permanent Stress slot.
Experiences. +1 to two Experiences.
Domain Card. An additional domain card of your level or lower (in tier 2, up to level 4).
Evasion. +1 Evasion.
Path Upgrade. Take your Path's next feature: Specialization at tier 2 or later, Mastery at tier 3 or later. Then cross out this tier's Multiclass option.
Augment Slot. One extra augment slot (or kit slot). Tier 2 and up.
Proficiency. +1 Proficiency. Costs both picks.
Multiclass. Level 5 and up; costs both picks. Choose a second Tradition, gain its class feature and one of its domains, and take the Foundation of one of its Paths. Cross out one unused Path Upgrade on this tier and every later Multiclass. You can multiclass once.

A multiclass domain gives you cards at half your level, rounded up: a level 5 Solo who multiclasses into Techie and takes Wire can choose Wire cards of level 3 or lower. Everything you do is still at your real level.

10Rules
Operator

The Roll

Roll two d12s, a Hope Die and a Fear Die. Add a trait, any Experiences you spent Hope on, and an advantage d6 (or take away a disadvantage d6). Meet the Difficulty to succeed.

Critical successBoth dice show the same number. You succeed even if the total missed, you gain a Hope, you clear a Stress, and an attack deals extra damage.
Success with HopeTotal meets the Difficulty, Hope Die higher. You get it clean. Gain a Hope.
Success with FearTotal meets the Difficulty, Fear Die higher. You get it, with a cost. The GM gains a Fear and makes a move.
Failure with HopeTotal misses, Hope Die higher. It didn't work, but you gain a Hope and the consequence is soft.
Failure with FearTotal misses, Fear Die higher. It goes wrong. The GM gains a Fear and makes a hard move.

Taking Damage

Compare the damage to your thresholds, which come from your armor plus your level. Below Major, mark 1 Hit Point. At Major, mark 2. At Severe, mark 3. Before you mark, you can spend one Armor Slot to drop the damage one step (Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to nothing). Your armor has slots equal to its Armor Score; they come back when you repair during a rest. Damage at double your Severe threshold marks 4 Hit Points. Some hits are just that bad.

Stress

Six slots to start. You mark Stress to power cards and gear, to accept a complication the GM offers, and when adversaries rattle you. When your last Stress is marked you become Vulnerable until you clear one. If you must mark Stress with none left, mark a Hit Point instead.

Hope

Hope is yours. You start each campaign with 2, hold up to 6, and spend it to: add an Experience to a roll (1 each), Help an Ally (1, they gain an advantage die), initiate a Tag Team roll with another PC (3, once per session), power your Tradition's Hope Feature (3), or power a card (Section A). Scars cross out Hope slots permanently.

Experiences

An Experience is a short phrase about who you've been, at +2. When a roll fits it, spend a Hope before rolling to add the bonus. You can spend on more than one Experience for one roll, a Hope each. You start with two and gain one at levels 2, 5, and 8, and more through advancements.

Starting Numbers

Copy your Tradition's Evasion and Hit Points. Everyone starts with 6 Stress, 2 Hope, and Proficiency 1. Your damage thresholds are your armor's plus your level.

11Rules
Operator

Rests

A short rest is an hour off the street: the van, a safehouse, a back room. Each PC takes two downtime moves: tend to wounds (clear 1d4 + tier HP, yours or an ally's), clear Stress (1d4 + tier), repair armor (1d4 + tier slots), or prepare (gain a Hope; 2 each if you prepare together). Three short rests, then the next must be long. A long rest is a night somewhere safe: you choose two moves, and each long-rest move clears everything of its kind (every Hit Point, every Stress, or every Armor Slot) or gains 2 Hope. Instead of a move, you can work on a project: a clan-fab build, an augment installed at a ripper, a dive arranged. Projects run on a countdown.

Death

When you mark your last Hit Point, you choose a death move. Blaze of Glory: one last action that critically succeeds, then you die. Avoid Death: you drop unconscious and the situation gets worse; roll your Hope Die, and if it's your level or lower you take a scar (cross out a Hope slot, permanently). Risk It All: roll the Duality Dice; Hope higher, you stay up and clear that many HP or Stress; Fear higher, you're gone; doubles, you clear everything. Lose your last Hope slot and the character's story ends at the close of the session.

Conditions

HiddenOut of sight, and nobody knows exactly where you are. Rolls against you have disadvantage. Ends when you attack, move into view, or get found.
RestrainedYou can't move, but you can act from where you are.
VulnerableRolls against you have advantage.
BlindedAttack rolls you make have disadvantage and you can't target anything beyond Very Close. Caused by flashbangs and the Blind load.
OfflineOne named augment or device doesn't work. Caused by EMP, Neurotox, and the Glitch load. Clear it with an action roll or a Detox Flush.
StuckRestrained by foam, web, or wire. Clear it with a Strength Roll (15) or solvent.
TracedA network's Consequence countdown hit zero: it knows where your body is, and its response is on the way. Clear it by jacking out and moving.
